items.why: Hold KB at chest, sit deep, elbows inside knees, chest tall

fields.release: Hold a kettlebell by the horns (sides of the handle) at chest level, close to your body. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width. Squat deep, keeping your chest tall and letting your elbows track inside your knees. Drive through your whole foot to stand back up. The goblet position naturally promotes good squat form.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes.

items.name: KB Halo
items.why: Circle KB around head, keep core tight, smooth path

fields.release: Hold a kettlebell upside down by the horns at chest level. Circle it around your head in a smooth path, keeping it close to your head and your core braced. Complete several reps in one direction, then switch. Keep your torso still and avoid leaning. This builds shoulder mobility and stability while engaging the core.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core.

levels.name: Half-Kneeling
levels.note: Kneel on one knee for stability

items.name: KB Snatch
items.why: One motion floor to overhead, punch through at top, lock out

fields.release: Swing the kettlebell from between your legs and, in one powerful motion, drive it overhead to a locked-out position. At the top, punch your hand through the handle so the bell rests gently against the back of your forearm. This combines a swing and an overhead press into one explosive movement. Master the swing and clean before attempting snatches.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, hips, core.

items.name: KB Swing
items.why: Hip hinge, snap hips forward, float the bell, arms are ropes

fields.release: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and the kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge at the hips, grab the bell, and hike it back between your legs. Explosively snap your hips forward to drive the kettlebell up to chest or shoulder height. Let it swing back between your legs and repeat. Your arms are just ropes; all the power comes from your hips.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, hamstrings, core.

items.name: KB Turkish Get-Up
items.why: Eyes on bell at all times, move through each position deliberately

fields.release: Lie on your back with a kettlebell pressed overhead in one hand. Move through a series of deliberate positions to transition from lying down to standing while keeping the bell locked out overhead. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell at all times. This is a full-body exercise that builds stability, mobility, and strength. Learn each position slowly before adding weight.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: full body.

items.name: KB Windmill
items.why: KB overhead, hinge sideways, eyes on bell, touch floor

fields.release: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and lock it out. Turn your feet slightly away from the loaded side. Keeping your eyes on the bell, hinge at the hips and slide your free hand down your front leg toward the floor. Your torso rotates open as you descend. Stand back up by driving through your hips. This challenges oblique strength, hip mobility, and shoulder stability.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, shoulders, hips.

items.name: Kick Check (Shin Block)
items.why: Lift leg to block with shin, toes pointed down, stay balanced

fields.release: From your fighting stance, lift your lead leg by bending the knee and turning the shin outward to block an incoming kick. Point your toes downward and raise your knee to at least waist height. Keep your hands up to protect your head and stay balanced on your supporting leg. Return to your stance quickly after the check.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hip flexors, calves.

items.name: Knee Strike
items.why: Drive knee upward, pull with hips, squeeze at top

fields.release: From your fighting stance, drive your rear or lead knee upward toward the imaginary target, pulling your hips into the strike. Rise onto the ball of your supporting foot and squeeze at the top of the motion. In a clinch position, you would pull the opponent into the knee. Keep your guard up and core engaged throughout the strike.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hip flexors, core.

items.name: Knee to wall
items.why: Re-test: Every 2 weeks. Higher is better.

fields.release: Big toe pointing at the wall, foot square. Slide the foot back until your knee only just touches the wall with the heel still down. Measure from the wall to the big toe. Same foot position, same bare feet, every time.
fields.notice: Recorded in cm.

items.name: Knee-to-chest pinch
items.why: Re-test: Every 2 weeks. Lower is better.

fields.release: On your back, draw one knee to your chest. Rate the PINCH at the front of the hip, 0 to 10 — not the stretch behind. Same depth each time, so stop at the point where the pinch first appears rather than pulling to end range.
fields.notice: Recorded in 0–10.

items.name: L-Sit
items.why: Hands on floor beside hips, lift legs parallel, lock arms

fields.release: Sit on the floor with legs straight in front of you and place your hands flat on the floor beside your hips. Lock your arms and press down to lift your entire body off the floor, holding your legs straight and parallel to the ground. This requires significant core, hip flexor, and tricep strength. Start with a tucked position if you cannot hold straight legs.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors.

levels.name: One Leg Extended
levels.note: Extend one leg at a time

items.name: Lat & back of armpit
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Lie on your side, arm overhead, ball in the back wall of the armpit. Small movements, not long rolls.
fields.load: Lat squeeze isometric — arms at your sides, squeeze the armpits down toward the hips, 5 sec ×10. Then assisted hang, feet partly down, 20–40 sec, pulling the shoulder blades DOWN.
fields.notice: Ribs stop flaring. Belly breath comes easier. Traps quieten.
fields.careful: If a shoulder subluxes or feels unstable overhead, keep the feet partly on the ground during hangs until the scapular base is solid.

photos.caption: Side-lying, arm overhead, in the back wall of the armpit. Small movements, not long rolls.

The load. Hang, then raise yourself a few inches WITHOUT bending the arms — a reverse shrug that depresses the shoulder blades. This is the "pull the blades DOWN" cue, and it is the exact drill rather than an approximation.

items.name: Lat Roll
items.why: Lie on side, roller under armpit, roll up and down lat

fields.release: Lie on your side with the foam roller positioned under your armpit area. Extend the bottom arm overhead and slowly roll from your armpit down to the bottom of your ribcage. Pause on tender areas for 20-30 seconds. Control pressure with your feet and opposite hand. This releases tightness in the lats, which improves overhead reach and shoulder mobility.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lats.

items.name: Lateral Bound
items.why: Push off one leg, land on the other, absorb and stick

fields.release: Stand on one leg, push off explosively to the side, and land on the opposite foot. Absorb the landing by bending your knee and hip, sticking the position for a moment before bounding back. Keep your hips and chest facing forward throughout. This builds lateral power, ankle stability, and single-leg landing mechanics.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, quads, ankles.

items.name: Lateral Lunge
items.why: Wide step to side, sit hips back, keep trailing leg straight

fields.release: Stand with feet together, then take a wide step to one side. Sit your hips back and bend the stepping leg while keeping the trailing leg straight. Push through the bent leg to return to the starting position. Keep your chest up and your weight in your heel on the working side. You should feel this in your inner thighs and glutes.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: adductors, quads, glutes.

levels.name: Cossack Squat
levels.note: Full depth, raised toes on straight leg

fields.release: Step wide to the right, bending right knee and pushing hips back while keeping left leg straight. Keep both feet flat. Sit into the bent knee side. Feel the stretch in the straight leg's inner thigh. Hold, then switch sides.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: adductors, groin, hamstrings, quads.

levels.name: easy
levels.note: Shallow lunge, hands on thigh for support

levels.name: advanced
levels.note: Transition into Cossack squat — heel on straight leg lifts

items.name: Lateral Raise
items.why: Slight bend in elbows, raise to shoulder height, control down

fields.release: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower slowly. Avoid swinging or using momentum, and do not raise above shoulder level. You should feel this in the sides of your shoulders.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders.

levels.name: Banded
levels.note: Use a light band for resistance

items.name: Leg Raise
items.why: Low back pressed to floor, raise legs to 90 degrees, lower slow

fields.release: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands at your sides or under your hips for support. Press your lower back firmly into the floor. Raise both legs together to 90 degrees, then lower them slowly toward the floor without letting your lower back arch up. If your back lifts off the floor, bend your knees slightly or do not lower your legs as far.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors.

items.name: Legs Up the Wall
items.why: Butt near wall, legs straight up, arms relaxed

fields.release: Sit with one hip against a wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back. Scoot your butt as close to the wall as comfortable. Arms at sides or on belly. Close your eyes. This inverts blood flow, calms the nervous system, and gently stretches hamstrings.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, lower back, nervous system.

levels.name: Away From Wall
levels.note: Butt a few inches from wall

levels.name: Straddle
levels.note: Straddle legs wide for adductor stretch

items.name: Lunge
items.why: Long step, knee hovers above floor, drive through front heel

fields.release: Stand tall and take a long step forward. Lower your body by bending both knees until your rear knee hovers just above the floor and your front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground. Drive through your front heel to return to standing. Keep your torso upright throughout and avoid letting your front knee shoot past your toes.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Mace 10-to-2
items.why: Swing mace like a pendulum from 10 o'clock to 2 o'clock

fields.release: Hold the mace at the end of the handle and swing it behind your head like a pendulum, moving the mace head from the 10 o'clock position to the 2 o'clock position and back. Keep your core braced and control the arc. This is a simpler variation of the 360 that builds the same shoulder endurance and grip strength with less range of motion.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core.

items.name: Mace 360
items.why: Swing mace behind head in full 360, tight core, control the arc

fields.release: Hold the mace at the end of the handle with both hands near your chest. Swing the mace head behind your head in a full 360-degree circle, controlling it as it passes behind your neck and back to the front. Keep your core tight and your elbows close to your head. The momentum of the mace head makes this a challenging shoulder and grip exercise.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core, grip.

items.name: Mace Barbarian Squat
items.why: Squat while pressing mace overhead, keep chest up

fields.release: Hold the mace at chest level and squat down while pressing the mace overhead. As you stand, bring the mace back to chest level. Keep your chest upright and core braced throughout. The offset weight of the mace challenges your stability more than a balanced weight would. This is a full-body compound movement.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, shoulders.

items.name: Mace Flow
items.why: Chain mace movements together in smooth continuous flow

fields.release: Link multiple mace exercises together into one continuous sequence without stopping. For example, combine a 360 into a grave digger into a paddle swing. Focus on smooth transitions between movements and maintaining control of the mace throughout. This builds shoulder endurance, coordination, and full-body conditioning. Start with two movements and add more as you gain confidence.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: full body.

items.name: Mace Grave Digger
items.why: Shovel-like motion, rotate through core, control the mace

fields.release: Hold the mace with a staggered grip and perform a diagonal shoveling motion, rotating through your core as if digging with a shovel. Drive the movement from your hips and core, not your arms. Control the mace through the entire range of motion. This builds rotational core strength and mimics real-world functional movements.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, core.

items.name: Mace Lunge + Reach
items.why: Lunge forward while reaching mace overhead or to the side

fields.release: Hold the mace in both hands and step into a lunge position. As you lunge, reach the mace overhead or rotate it to one side to add an upper-body and core challenge to the lower-body movement. The offset weight of the mace creates an additional stability demand. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes and your torso upright.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, shoulders.

items.name: Mace Paddle Swing
items.why: Swing mace side to side like paddling, rotate from hips

fields.release: Hold the mace with a staggered grip and swing it from side to side in a paddling motion, as if paddling a canoe. Rotate through your hips and core to drive each swing. Keep the movement smooth and controlled. This targets the obliques and builds rotational endurance. Switch your grip and dominant side each set.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, core.

items.name: Mace Uppercut
items.why: Drive mace upward in uppercut motion, rotate and brace

fields.release: Hold the mace with a staggered grip and drive it upward in an uppercut-like motion, rotating your hips and core to generate power. Brace your core as you punch the mace head upward. Control the mace as you return to the starting position. This combines rotational core work with shoulder and arm engagement.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: core, shoulders.

items.name: Median nerve glide
items.dose: 10 reps × 2 sets per side.
items.why: Different tissue, different rules. Some of what reads as muscle tightness is neural.

fields.release: Arm out to the side at shoulder height, elbow bent, palm facing up near your shoulder. Straighten the elbow out to the side while bending the wrist back so the fingers point down and behind you — and at the same time tilt your head AWAY from that arm. Reverse: bend the elbow back in, relax the wrist, and tilt your head TOWARD the arm. Slow and smooth, about 2 seconds each way.
fields.notice: Arm symptoms that come and go with position are usually neural rather than muscular. This tests that directly.
fields.careful: Given the thoracic outlet picture, start with a much smaller range than feels necessary. If it reproduces numbness or tingling, halve the range. Never push into symptoms.

photos.caption: The arm and wrist position. Yours is a GLIDE, not this held stretch — move in and out continuously, about 2 seconds each way, and never park at the end position.

items.name: Meditation
items.why: Even 5 minutes reduces cortisol and improves focus

items.name: Mid & upper back
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Roller across the mid-back, arms crossed over the chest. A few passes, then park on a stiff segment and drape backwards over it. Breathe into it. Don't crank.
fields.load: Cat-cow ×8 with real attention to the cow — that's the direction you've lost. Then prone Y-raises ×10, light.
fields.notice: Standing tall stops being effort. Head sits back over the shoulders.
fields.careful: Extend from the mid-back, not the low back. If it hinges down low, move the roller up.

photos.caption: Roller across the mid-back, arms crossed over the chest. Park on a stiff segment and drape back over it.
Cat-cow. Give real attention to the cow direction — that is the one you have lost.

items.name: Morning sunlight 10 min
items.why: Sets circadian rhythm, boosts vitamin D, improves sleep

items.name: Mountain Climber
items.why: Plank position, drive knees to chest, hips low and stable

fields.release: Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders. Rapidly drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs in a running motion while keeping your hips low and stable. Avoid letting your hips bounce up and down. The faster you go, the more cardiovascular demand. Keep your core braced to maintain a flat back throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors.

items.name: Movement 20–30 min
items.why: Lymph needs muscle movement — walk, bike, play, anything counts

items.name: Muay Thai Stance + Movement
items.why: Tall stance, hands high, weight on balls of feet, stay balanced

fields.release: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, dominant foot slightly back. Keep your hands high near your temples with elbows pointed down to protect your ribs. Stay on the balls of your feet with weight evenly distributed. Unlike boxing, the Muay Thai stance is more upright to facilitate kicking and knee strikes. Practice moving forward, back, and laterally.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves, core.

items.name: Muscle-Up
items.why: Explosive pull, transition over bar, press to lockout

fields.release: Hang from a pull-up bar and perform an explosive pull-up, generating enough height to transition your chest over the bar. Once above the bar, press your body up to a straight-arm support position. This is an advanced movement that combines a pull-up and a dip. Build the prerequisite strength with high pull-ups and chest-to-bar pull-ups first.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lats, chest, triceps.

items.name: Neck Stretch
items.why: Tilt ear to shoulder, keep opposite shoulder down

fields.release: Sit or stand tall. Tilt right ear toward right shoulder. Gently place right hand on top of head for light overpressure. Keep left shoulder down. Hold 15-20 seconds. For the front of the neck, look up and slightly to one side. Switch sides.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: neck, upper traps.

levels.name: Nerve Glides
levels.note: All positions with gentle nerve glides

items.name: Neck-crack urge
items.why: Re-test: Count on a normal day, monthly. Lower is better.

fields.release: Rough count of how many times in a day you want to crack your neck. Count the urge, not the act. This is the behaviour the base-of-skull work is meant to replace.
fields.notice: Recorded in /day.

items.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
items.why: Anchor feet, slowly lower body forward, fight with hamstrings

fields.release: Kneel on the floor with your feet anchored under something heavy or held by a partner. Keeping your body straight from knees to head, slowly lower yourself forward toward the floor by extending at the knees while resisting with your hamstrings. Lower as far as you can with control, then push yourself back up from the floor. This is an extremely difficult hamstring exercise; start with negatives only.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings.

levels.name: Negative Only
levels.note: Slow lower, push up from floor

items.name: Nose only, all day
items.dose: All day, imperfectly. It is a default you are rebuilding, not a rule you are passing or failing.
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.release: Mouth closed at rest. Lips sealed, teeth slightly apart, tongue on the roof of the mouth. Nose breathing on walks. If you have to open your mouth, slow down until you do not. Notice when you break the seal. Stress, concentration, and reaching for something are the usual triggers.
fields.notice: Reaching for the mouth constantly is data, not failure — it points at nasal obstruction, which is already on your list.
fields.careful: Do not tape your mouth at night. That advice is everywhere in this space and it is specifically wrong for you: you can reproduce your own airway collapse, and taping removes the escape route.

items.name: Nose-only walk
items.why: Re-test: Monthly. Higher is better.

fields.release: Walking at a normal pace, time until you have to open your mouth. Flat ground, same route. This one is as much a readout on nasal obstruction as on fitness.
fields.notice: Recorded in min.

items.name: Oil pulling
items.why: Swish coconut oil 10–20 min — oral microbiome support

items.name: Pallof Press
items.why: Press band straight out from chest, resist rotation

fields.release: Anchor a resistance band at chest height to your side. Hold the band at your chest with both hands and stand or kneel perpendicular to the anchor. Press the band straight out in front of you and hold, resisting the rotational pull of the band. Return to your chest and repeat. This trains your core anti-rotation muscles, which are essential for athletic performance and spinal health.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: core, anti-rotation.

items.name: Parallel Bar Dip
items.why: Elbows back, lean forward for chest emphasis, full depth

fields.release: Grip a set of parallel bars and support your body with arms locked out. Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are at least parallel to the floor, then press back up to lockout. Lean forward to place more emphasis on your chest, or stay upright to target your triceps. Avoid shrugging your shoulders at the bottom.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, triceps, shoulders.

items.name: Parallel Bar L-Sit
items.why: Lock arms, lift legs parallel to floor, point toes

fields.release: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms fully locked out. Lift your legs straight in front of you until they are parallel to the floor and hold this position. Point your toes and keep your arms straight. This demands significant core and hip flexor strength. Start with a tucked position if holding straight legs is too difficult.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors, triceps.

levels.name: One Leg Extended
levels.note: Extend one leg at a time

items.name: Parallel Bar Swing
items.why: Controlled swing, tight core, shoulders stable

fields.release: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms locked out. Initiate a controlled forward and backward swinging motion using your core and shoulders. Keep your body tight and maintain stable shoulders throughout. This builds shoulder stability and body control, and serves as a foundation for more advanced parallel bar skills.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core.

items.name: Pec / Shoulder Roll
items.why: Face down, roller under chest/shoulder, roll gently

fields.release: Lie face down at a slight angle with the foam roller under the front of one shoulder and chest area. Use your feet and opposite arm to control pressure and slowly roll across the pec and front deltoid area. Pause on any tender spots and breathe into them. This is especially beneficial for people who sit at desks or have rounded shoulder posture.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: pecs, anterior deltoids.

items.name: Pigeon Stretch
items.why: Front shin across body, square hips, ease into stretch

fields.release: From a kneeling position, bring one shin across your body in front of you with the knee angled outward. Extend your other leg straight behind you. Square your hips toward the front and ease your torso down toward the floor. You should feel a deep stretch in the front hip and glute. Use your hands for support and breathe into the stretch.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: glutes, hip flexors, piriformis.

items.name: Pike Push-Up
items.why: Hips high, head between arms, touch nose to floor

fields.release: Start in a downward-dog position with your hips piked high and hands shoulder-width apart. Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands, then press back up. Keep your hips high throughout so the movement targets your shoulders rather than your chest. You should feel this primarily in your front and side deltoids.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, triceps.

levels.name: Feet Elevated Pike
levels.note: Feet on bench for steeper angle

items.name: Pistol Squat
items.why: One leg extended forward, sit all the way down and stand

fields.release: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended straight in front of you. Lower yourself by bending the standing leg until you reach the bottom of a full squat, then drive back up to standing. Keep your extended leg off the floor throughout. This demands significant single-leg strength, balance, and ankle mobility. Use a support or box to build up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, ankle stability.

levels.name: Negative Only
levels.note: Slow lower, stand with both legs

items.name: Plank
items.why: Straight line from head to heels, squeeze everything tight

fields.release: Get into a forearm plank position with elbows directly under shoulders and feet together or hip-width apart. Your body should form a perfectly straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your abs, glutes, and quads to maintain the position. Avoid letting your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. Breathe steadily throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, obliques, shoulders.

items.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
items.why: Lie face down, lift arms in Y, T, then W shapes

fields.release: Lie face down on the floor with arms extended. Lift your arms off the ground into a Y shape (overhead and angled out), then a T shape (straight out to the sides), then a W shape (elbows bent, pulled toward ribs). Hold each position for a beat. These target the upper back, rear delts, and rotator cuff muscles important for posture.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: upper back, rear delts.

items.name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
items.why: Hands by waist, lean forward, protract shoulders at top

fields.release: Set up in a push-up position but place your hands further back, near your waist, with fingers pointing forward or slightly outward. Lean your body forward over your hands and perform push-ups from this position. Push your shoulder blades apart (protract) at the top of each rep. This variation heavily loads the shoulders and core.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, shoulders, core.

items.name: Pull-Up
items.why: Full dead hang to chin over bar, no kipping

fields.release: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Start from a full dead hang with arms completely straight. Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, then lower back to a full dead hang. Avoid swinging or kipping; the movement should be smooth and controlled. Engage your lats by thinking about pulling your elbows down to your hips.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lats, biceps, forearms.

levels.name: Weighted
levels.note: Add weight via backpack or DB

items.name: Push-Up
items.why: Chest to floor, full lockout, body in straight line

fields.release: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, body forming a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest to the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension. Keep your core tight and avoid letting your hips sag or pike up. You should feel the work in your chest, shoulders, and triceps.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, shoulders, triceps.

levels.name: Archer Push-Up
levels.note: One arm extended to the side

items.name: Quad Roll
items.why: Face down, roller under thighs, roll from hip to knee

fields.release: Lie face down in a forearm plank position with the foam roller under the front of your thighs. Roll slowly from your hips down to just above your knees, pausing on tender areas. Support yourself with your forearms and control the pressure with your arms. For more pressure, stack one leg on top of the other to roll one quad at a time.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads.

levels.name: Cross-Friction
levels.note: Rock side to side on tight spots

items.name: Renegade Row
items.why: Plank on DBs, row one arm at a time, minimize hip rotation

fields.release: Get into a high plank position with each hand gripping a dumbbell on the floor. With a wide foot stance for stability, row one dumbbell up to your hip by pulling your elbow past your torso, then lower and repeat on the other side. The key is minimizing hip rotation as you row. Keep your core braced tight and avoid rocking side to side.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: back, core.

items.name: Romanian Deadlift
items.why: Soft knees, hinge at hips, slide DBs along legs, flat back

fields.release: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding dumbbells in front of your thighs. With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the hips and push your butt back, sliding the dumbbells down along your legs. Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat throughout. Squeeze your glutes to drive your hips forward and return to standing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, glutes, lower back.

items.name: Roundhouse Kick
items.why: Turn hip over, kick through target with shin, pivot base foot

fields.release: From your fighting stance, pivot on your base foot while turning your hip over and swinging your leg in a circular arc, striking with your shin. Your base foot should rotate so your toes point away from the target. Keep your hands up and swing your arm on the kicking side slightly back for counterbalance. The power comes from the hip rotation, not just the leg.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hips, quads, obliques.

items.name: Russian Twist
items.why: Lean back, rotate torso side to side, keep chest up

fields.release: Sit on the floor with knees bent and lean your torso back about 45 degrees. Clasp your hands together or hold a weight in front of your chest. Rotate your torso to tap your hands on the floor beside each hip, alternating sides. Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your back. Lift your feet off the floor for an added challenge.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques.

items.name: Scapular Push-Up
items.why: Arms locked, only shoulder blades move — protract and retract

fields.release: Get into a high plank position with arms fully locked out. Without bending your elbows, let your chest sink between your shoulder blades (retract), then push the floor away and round your upper back (protract). Only your shoulder blades should move. This exercise strengthens the serratus anterior and improves shoulder stability.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: serratus anterior, shoulders.

items.name: Sciatic glide
items.dose: 10 reps × 2 sets per side. Daily is fine.
items.why: Different tissue, different rules. Some of what reads as muscle tightness is neural.

fields.release: Sit on the edge of a chair with your hands on your thighs. Slouch. Let your low back round. This is deliberate, not sloppy. Now, at the same time: straighten one knee out in front of you AND tip your head BACK. Then reverse, at the same time: bend the knee back down AND drop your chin to your chest. That is one rep. About 2 seconds each direction, smooth and continuous.
fields.notice: If your hamstring range improves from this when stretching has not moved it, the restriction was never muscular. A pull down the back of the leg that MOVES as you go. That movement is the nerve sliding, which is the whole point.
fields.careful: This is flossing, not stretching — never hold the end position. If it reproduces pain, tingling, or numbness, reduce the range until it does not. More is not better here; this is one of the few drills where overdoing it clearly makes things worse.

items.name: Scorpion Stretch
items.why: Lying face down, reach foot toward opposite hand behind you

fields.release: Lie face down with arms extended out to the sides. Lift one leg and reach it across your body toward the opposite hand behind you, rotating through your hips and thoracic spine. Keep the opposite shoulder pressed into the floor. Return to the start and repeat on the other side. This opens up the hip flexors and thoracic spine simultaneously.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hip flexors, thoracic spine, chest.

items.name: Screen-free wind-down
items.why: No screens 30–60 min before bed — protects melatonin production

items.name: Seated Forward Fold
items.why: Sit with legs extended, hinge at hips, reach for toes

fields.release: Sit with legs extended straight in front of you. Sit tall first, then hinge at the hips and reach toward your toes. Keep your back as flat as possible — don't round excessively. Use a strap around feet if needed. Breathe and relax deeper on each exhale.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, lower back, calves.

items.name: Shadowbox Round
items.why: Stay light on feet, mix punches, movement, and defense

fields.release: Shadowboxing is practicing punches, kicks, movement, and defense against an imaginary opponent. Stay light on your feet, keep your hands up, and mix combinations of strikes with footwork and head movement. Visualize an opponent in front of you and react to imaginary attacks. This builds technique, endurance, and coordination.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: full body.

items.name: Shoulder CARs
items.why: Fist tight, move arm in biggest circle possible, stay controlled

fields.release: Stand tall and make a tight fist with one hand. Slowly raise your arm in front of you, continue overhead, then behind you and back down, tracing the biggest circle possible with a straight arm. Move very slowly and with control. Repeat in the opposite direction. This helps maintain shoulder mobility and highlights any restrictions in your range of motion.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: shoulders, rotator cuff.

items.name: Shoulder Tap
items.why: Minimize hip rotation, keep hips square to floor

fields.release: Start in a high plank position with hands directly under shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width apart. Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then return it to the floor and repeat on the other side. The key challenge is keeping your hips perfectly still and square to the floor; widen your stance to make this easier.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core.

items.name: Side Plank
items.why: Stack feet, hips high, straight line from head to ankles

fields.release: Lie on your side and prop yourself up on your forearm with your elbow directly under your shoulder. Stack your feet and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to ankles. Hold this position, keeping your hips high. Avoid letting your hips drop toward the floor. You should feel this in your obliques and the side of your hip.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, shoulders.

levels.name: Copenhagen
levels.note: Top foot on bench, bottom leg free

items.name: Side-lying rib opener
items.equipment: Foam roller or a rolled towel
items.dose: 8 breaths per side. Daily if you like it.
items.why: This works what pulls on the rib cage, not the cage itself.

fields.tool: Foam roller or a rolled towel
fields.release: Lie on your side with the roller under your bottom ribs, running across your body. Stretch the top arm overhead and bring the top leg forward for balance. Breathe INTO the upside ribs — the ones facing the ceiling. Feel them open. 8 breaths, then swap sides.
fields.notice: Rotation and side-bending get easier. Pairs naturally with the lat work.
fields.careful: Roller under the ribs, not the waist. If it presses into soft belly, move it up.

photos.caption: Side-lying with the top arm overhead. Yours adds a roller under the bottom ribs and eight breaths into the upside ribs.

items.name: Single leg, eyes closed
items.why: Re-test: Every 2 weeks. Higher is better.

fields.release: Barefoot, counter within reach. Stop the clock the moment the foot moves or you touch down. Cap it at 60 — past that it is measuring patience, not balance.
fields.notice: Recorded in sec.

items.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
items.why: One foot, full stretch at bottom, peak squeeze at top

fields.release: Stand on one foot, ideally on the edge of a step so your heel can drop below the surface. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing your calf at the top, then lower slowly below step level for a full stretch. Hold a wall or railing for balance. This isolates one calf at a time for better strength development.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves.

items.name: Single-Leg Hop
items.why: One leg, controlled hop, soft landing, stay balanced

fields.release: Stand on one leg and hop in a controlled manner, landing softly on the same foot each time. Keep your knee slightly bent and focus on balance and a quiet landing. This builds single-leg power, ankle stability, and proprioception. Start with small hops in place and progress to forward, lateral, and multi-directional hops.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves, quads, ankles.

items.name: Single-leg progression
items.equipment: Bare feet, and a wall or counter within reach
items.dose: 5 minutes, most days. Barefoot always.
items.why: Proprioception training — the direct route to knowing where your body is and what it is doing.

fields.tool: Bare feet, and a wall or counter within reach
fields.release: Only move up a level when the current one is boring.
fields.notice: Your foot will be visibly working — toes gripping, arch adjusting constantly. That is the foot-to-brain conversation you are trying to restart.
fields.careful: Stay within reach of a counter. The Level 3 head turns can trigger dizziness given the dysautonomia — if the room moves, sit down and come back to it another day at a slower speed.

levels.name: Single leg, eyes closed, 15–30 seconds
levels.note: This is a big jump; vision was doing most of the work.

Single leg on the pillow, eyes closed

items.name: Sissy Squat
items.why: Lean back, knees forward, lower on toes, keep hips extended

fields.release: Stand on your toes with your body upright. Lean your torso back while pushing your knees far forward, lowering yourself toward the ground. Keep your hips fully extended throughout so your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. Use a support for balance while learning. This intensely isolates the quads.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads.

items.name: Skater Squat
items.why: Single leg, rear knee taps floor behind you, arms for balance

fields.release: Stand on one leg with the other leg bent behind you, knee pointing down. Lower yourself by bending the standing leg until your rear knee gently taps the floor, then stand back up. Extend your arms in front for counterbalance. This is a challenging single-leg exercise that builds quad and glute strength. Hold onto a support while learning.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes.

levels.name: To Box
levels.note: Lower to a box or target

items.name: Skipping for Height
items.why: Drive knee up, push off hard, get maximum height each skip

fields.release: Skip forward with an emphasis on getting as high off the ground as possible with each skip. Drive your knee explosively upward and push hard off the ground with your opposite foot. Pump your arms to generate additional height. This develops explosive hip extension and improves vertical power for jumping sports.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves, quads.

items.name: Sleep routine
items.why: Consistent bedtime, cool room, dark environment

items.name: Slip + Roll
items.why: Move head off centerline, slip to each side, roll under

fields.release: From your boxing stance, practice moving your head off the centerline to avoid imaginary punches. To slip, bend slightly at the waist to move your head to one side. To roll, bend your knees and rotate under an imaginary hook. Keep your hands up and eyes forward throughout. Start slowly and focus on staying balanced during each movement.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: core, quads.

items.name: Soft palate & throat
items.dose: Daily. Fold it into brushing your teeth so you do not have to remember it separately.
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.release: Say an exaggerated 'ahh' and hold it, feeling the back of the throat lift. ×10. Gargle water properly and loudly for 30 seconds. ×3. Aggressive enough that your eyes water slightly. Hum on a low pitch with a long exhale until you feel the buzz in your throat and chest.
fields.notice: Doubles as direct vagal work — the vagus nerve supplies the larynx. It is also relevant to the voice thread.
fields.careful: Nothing to speak of. This is the safest thing in the whole document.

items.name: Split Squat Jump
items.why: Lunge position, jump and switch legs mid-air, land soft

fields.release: Start in a lunge position with one foot forward and the other back. Explosively jump upward and switch your legs mid-air, landing in a lunge with the opposite foot forward. Land softly with your knees bent, keeping your torso upright. Avoid letting your back knee slam into the ground on landing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes.

items.name: Sprint Drill (Wall Drive)
items.why: Hands on wall, lean forward, drive knees alternating

fields.release: Place your hands on a wall at about chest height and lean forward at roughly a 45-degree angle with your body in a straight line. Alternately drive your knees toward the wall, focusing on a powerful hip extension on the push-off leg and a quick knee drive on the other. This drill teaches proper sprint mechanics and develops hip drive power.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, hip flexors.

items.name: Squat
items.why: Knees track over toes, hips below parallel, chest up

fields.release: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower your body as if sitting into a chair, going at least until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Squat Jump
items.why: Sit back, explode up, land soft, immediately reload

fields.release: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Lower into a squat, then explode upward as high as you can, swinging your arms for momentum. Land softly with bent knees, absorbing the impact, and immediately lower into the next squat to reload. Focus on both the height of your jump and the quality of your landing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes.

items.name: Squat support needed
items.why: Re-test: Monthly. Higher is better.

fields.release: Deep squat hold. 0 = arms carrying most of you. 1 = a firm pull. 2 = light fingers. 3 = hands off entirely. This is the progression — not depth.
fields.notice: Recorded in 0–3.

items.name: Standing Forward Fold
items.why: Hinge at hips, let gravity pull you down, relax neck

fields.release: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Hinge at the hips and fold your torso forward, letting gravity pull you down. Relax your neck and let your arms hang heavy. Bend your knees slightly if your hamstrings are tight. Breathe deeply and allow yourself to sink a little deeper into the stretch with each exhale. You should feel this in your hamstrings and lower back.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hamstrings, lower back, calves.

items.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
items.why: Foot on low surface, hinge forward with flat back

fields.release: Place one foot on a low step or bench (or just extend in front of you). Keep the elevated leg straight. Hinge at the hips and lean forward with a flat back until you feel the stretch behind the thigh. Keep hips square. Hold and switch.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, calves.

levels.name: Low Surface
levels.note: Foot on low surface, slight lean

levels.name: Bench Height
levels.note: Foot on bench height, deeper lean

levels.name: Flex Foot
levels.note: Flex foot, pull toes toward you

items.name: Standing Quad Stretch
items.why: Stand on one leg, pull heel toward glute

fields.release: Stand on one leg (hold wall if needed). Bend the other knee and grab your foot behind you, pulling heel toward glute. Keep knees close together and push hips slightly forward. You should feel the stretch in the front of your thigh.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, hip flexors.

levels.name: Backbend
levels.note: Add slight backbend for deeper hip flexor stretch

items.name: Step-Up
items.why: Drive through top foot, minimal push from bottom leg

fields.release: Stand facing a box or sturdy step. Place one foot fully on top of the box. Drive through the top foot to step up, bringing your body to a standing position on the box. Avoid pushing off with your bottom foot. Step down with control. Keep your torso upright and use a box height that allows your knee to bend to about 90 degrees.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes.

items.name: Strength training
items.why: Build muscle, support metabolism, improve bone density

items.name: Stretch/yoga 10+ min
items.why: Circulation + stress reduction

items.name: Suitcase Carry
items.why: DB in one hand, stand tall, resist leaning to that side

fields.release: Hold a dumbbell in one hand at your side and walk forward with an upright posture. The challenge is resisting the pull of the weight, which tries to make you lean sideways. Keep your shoulders level and core braced throughout. This builds oblique strength, grip endurance, and teaches your core to resist lateral forces.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, core, forearms.

items.name: Superman
items.why: Lift arms and legs off floor, squeeze glutes and back

fields.release: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight. Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor by squeezing your glutes and lower back muscles. Hold briefly at the top, then lower with control. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor rather than cranking your head up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lower back, glutes.

levels.name: Hold
levels.note: Static hold, arms and legs up

levels.name: Reverse Snow Angel
levels.note: Sweep arms from front to hips

levels.name: W-Raise
levels.note: Pull elbows down into W shape

fields.release: Lie on your back. Cross right ankle over left knee (making a "4" shape). Reach through and pull the left thigh toward your chest. You should feel a deep stretch in the right glute/hip. Keep head on the floor. Hold and switch.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: glutes, piriformis, hips.

levels.name: easy
levels.note: Keep bottom foot on floor, just cross ankle

levels.name: advanced
levels.note: Press crossed knee away while pulling thigh closer

items.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
items.why: Lie on back, lift one leg, hold behind thigh or calf

fields.release: Lie on your back. Lift one leg and hold behind the thigh or calf (use a towel or strap if needed). Keep the leg as straight as possible. Keep the other leg flat on the floor. Pull gently to deepen the stretch. Hold and breathe.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings.

levels.name: Deeper
levels.note: Pull closer, point/flex foot for different fibers

items.name: Supine Spinal Twist
items.why: Lie on back, pull knee across body, keep shoulders down

fields.release: Lie on your back, arms in a T. Pull one knee to chest, then guide it across your body to the opposite side. Let gravity pull the knee toward the floor. Keep both shoulders pressed down. Look in the opposite direction of the knee. Breathe and melt into it.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: spine, obliques, glutes, chest.

levels.name: Easy Twist
levels.note: Knee does not need to touch floor

levels.name: Full Twist
levels.note: Both shoulders stay down, breathe into twist

levels.name: Straight Leg
levels.note: Straighten crossing leg for deeper twist

items.name: Sweat session
items.why: Skin = detox organ — sauna, hot bath, or intense exercise

items.name: Teep (Front Kick)
items.why: Chamber knee, push ball of foot forward, snap back quick

fields.release: From your fighting stance, lift your knee toward your chest (chamber), then push the ball of your foot straight forward like you are pushing a door open. Snap your foot back quickly to the chambered position before returning to stance. This is a push kick used to create distance. Keep your guard up and core tight throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hip flexors, quads, core.

items.name: Thoracic Spine Extension (Roller)
items.why: Roller under upper back, extend over it, open chest

fields.release: Place the foam roller under your upper back, perpendicular to your spine. Support your head with your hands and keep your hips on the floor. Extend your upper back over the roller, letting your chest open up toward the ceiling. Move the roller to different positions along your upper back to target different segments. This counteracts the hunched posture from sitting.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: thoracic spine.

items.name: Thoracic Spine Rotation
items.why: Lock hips, rotate through upper back only, reach and open

fields.release: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked. Keeping your hips locked in place, rotate your upper back to open your top arm toward the floor on the other side. Return to the starting position. The key is isolating the rotation to your thoracic spine while your hips stay still. This is especially beneficial if you sit for long periods.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: thoracic spine, obliques.

levels.name: Open Book
levels.note: Lying on side, open top arm

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.why: On all fours, reach one arm under body and rotate, then open up

fields.release: Start on all fours. Reach one arm under your body and across to the other side, letting your shoulder and head rest on the floor as you rotate. Then reverse the motion and open that arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your thoracic spine in the opposite direction. Move slowly and breathe into the stretch. Alternate sides.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: thoracic spine, shoulders.

items.name: Tibialis Raise
items.why: Lean back against wall, lift toes toward shins

fields.release: Lean your back against a wall with your feet about a foot away from the wall. Lift your toes and the balls of your feet off the ground toward your shins, keeping your heels on the floor. Lower with control. This strengthens the tibialis anterior muscle on the front of the shin, which is important for ankle stability and preventing shin splints.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: tibialis anterior.

levels.name: Single-Leg
levels.note: One foot at a time for ankle strength

items.name: Toe control
items.dose: Daily. It takes two minutes and you can do it sitting down.
items.why: Proprioception training — the direct route to knowing where your body is and what it is doing.

fields.release: TOE SPREAD — spread all your toes apart without curling them. Hold 5 seconds. ×10. BIG TOE LIFT — press the other four toes down and lift only the big toe. Then reverse: big toe down, lift the other four. TOWEL SCRUNCH — towel flat on the floor, use your toes to drag it toward you. ×10 each foot. The lifts will be close to impossible at first. That is the point — it is a connection you do not have yet.
fields.notice: Individual toe control is a direct readout of the nerve pathway you are trying to rebuild. Watching it go from impossible to easy is the clearest progress marker in this entire document.
fields.careful: Cramping is common at first. Stop, stretch the foot out, come back tomorrow.

items.name: Toes-to-Bar
items.why: Controlled raise, touch toes to bar, no excessive swing

fields.release: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended. Engage your core and raise your legs, keeping them as straight as possible, until your toes touch the bar. Lower with control, minimizing any swing. This is an advanced core exercise; begin with knee raises or straight-leg raises to build the necessary strength and control.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors.

items.name: Tongue posture
items.dose: All day, as a default you keep returning to.
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.release: The whole tongue — not just the tip — suctioned flat against the roof of the mouth. Tip rests on the ridge just BEHIND your top front teeth, not on the teeth themselves. Lips sealed, teeth slightly apart, breathing through the nose. That is the resting position. Everything else in this section is training you toward holding it without thinking about it.
fields.notice: You already use this deliberately as an airway compensation. The goal is making it automatic, including while asleep, which is where it would actually help the collapse.
fields.careful: Jaw tension means you are pressing with the jaw instead of the tongue. Teeth stay apart.

items.name: Tongue press & suction
items.dose: 5–10 minutes daily, split however suits you. Give it 2–3 months before judging whether it works.
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.release: PRESS — whole tongue flat against the roof of the mouth, push up hard. Hold 10 seconds. ×10. SUCTION HOLD — suction the whole tongue flat to the palate so it makes a vacuum. Keeping that seal, slowly open your jaw as wide as you can WITHOUT the tongue peeling off. Hold 5 seconds, then close. ×10. SLIDE — tip of the tongue on the ridge behind the top front teeth, then slide it backwards along the roof of the mouth as far as it will go. ×10. STRONG SWALLOW — anchor the tongue tip on that ridge and swallow, pressing the tongue up hard through the whole swallow. ×10.
fields.notice: Waking less dry-mouthed. Tongue posture starting to hold without attention. Effects on sleep take months, not days — this is the slowest-acting thing in this document and also one of the highest-value. Your tongue gets tired, which tells you it was weak.
fields.careful: Jaw fatigue is expected; jaw pain is not. Given the TMJ picture, go easy on the wide-open suction hold and cut the range right back if the joint complains.

items.name: Typewriter Pull-Up
items.why: Pull up, shift weight side to side at top

fields.release: Perform a pull-up with a wide grip. At the top, shift your body weight toward one hand while keeping the other arm extended along the bar, then slide across to the other side before lowering. This is an advanced exercise that builds unilateral pulling strength. Master standard wide-grip pull-ups before attempting.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lats, biceps.

levels.name: Archer Pull-Up
levels.note: Pull to one hand, other arm straight

items.name: Under the rib margin
items.equipment: Your fingers. There is no tool for this
items.dose: 3 breaths per spot, 4–5 spots per side. Every other day.
items.why: This works what pulls on the rib cage, not the cage itself.

fields.tool: Your fingers. There is no tool for this
fields.release: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Let your belly go completely soft. Find the bottom edge of your rib cage at the front, starting near the centre just below the breastbone. Hook your fingertips gently just UNDER the rib margin, pointing up and in, toward your head. Exhale slowly. As you exhale, let your fingers sink slightly further under the edge. Hold there as you inhale. Do not dig and do not push against the breath. 3 breaths. Move about an inch outward along the rib arch and repeat. Work from the centre out to the side, then do the other side.
fields.notice: Belly breath comes without effort afterwards. This is the most direct access you have to the muscle itself, and the psoas attaches into the same lumbar fascia — your best release and your main symptom are literally continuous tissue. Deep and uncomfortable, occasionally oddly emotional. It should never be sharp.
fields.careful: Not on a full stomach. Gentle — you are reaching under the ribs near organs, and patience works far better than pressure. Sharp pain means stop.

items.name: Uppercut
items.why: Drop slightly, drive fist upward with legs and hips

fields.release: From your boxing stance, bend your knees slightly to dip, then drive your fist upward in a compact vertical arc, rotating your hips and driving up through your legs. Keep the punching arm close to your body and your other hand up guarding your chin. The power comes from your legs and hip rotation, not just your arm.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, biceps, core.

items.name: Vertical Jump Practice
items.why: Dip and drive arms, jump as high as possible, reach at peak

fields.release: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Quickly dip into a quarter squat while swinging your arms back, then explosively jump as high as possible, swinging your arms upward and reaching at the peak. Land softly with bent knees. Focus on maximum effort each rep, resting fully between jumps. Mark a spot on the wall to track your progress.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, calves.

levels.name: Approach
levels.note: Add a step into the jump

items.name: Waking dry mouth
items.why: Re-test: Weekly, first thing. Lower is better.

fields.release: 0 = none. 1 = slight. 2 = clearly dry. 3 = unpleasant. Crude, but it is one of the few home readouts on whether the tongue work is reaching sleep — and that takes months, so the record matters more than any single morning.
fields.notice: Recorded in 0–3.

items.name: Wall angel
items.why: Re-test: Monthly. Higher is better.

fields.release: Back to the wall, low back flat and held flat. Slide the arms up. 0 = forearms nowhere near. 1 = wrists touch. 2 = forearms touch but the back arches. 3 = forearms stay on the wall with the back flat.
fields.notice: Recorded in 0–3.

items.name: Wall Calf Stretch
items.why: Step back, press heel into floor, lean into wall

fields.release: Stand facing a wall. Step one foot back, keeping it straight with heel pressed into floor. Lean into the wall, bending the front knee. Feel the stretch in the back calf. For soleus (deeper calf), slightly bend the back knee while keeping heel down.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves, achilles.

levels.name: Both Versions
levels.note: Both versions (straight + bent knee), 15 sec each

items.name: Wall Sit
items.why: Back flat on wall, thighs parallel to floor, hold

fields.release: Stand with your back flat against a wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, knees bent at 90 degrees. Keep your back pressed firmly against the wall and your feet flat on the floor. Hold this position for as long as you can. You should feel a deep burn in your quads. Avoid placing your hands on your thighs for support.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads.

items.name: Wall Slide
items.why: Back and arms flat on wall, slide arms up and down

fields.release: Stand with your back flat against a wall, feet about six inches away. Place the back of your hands and forearms against the wall at shoulder height. Slowly slide your arms up overhead while keeping your back, hands, and forearms in contact with the wall, then slide back down. If anything loses wall contact, you have limited mobility in that range.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: upper back, shoulders, posture.

items.name: Woodchop
items.why: Rotate from hips, arms follow torso, control the motion

fields.release: Anchor a resistance band low or high to one side. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and grab the band with both hands. Rotate your torso to pull the band diagonally across your body in a chopping motion, pivoting at your hips. Control the return. The power comes from your hips and core, not your arms. Keep your arms relatively straight throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: obliques, core.

items.name: World's Greatest Stretch
items.why: Lunge, plant hand, rotate and reach to sky, feel every part open

fields.release: Step into a deep lunge position and plant the hand on the same side as your front foot on the floor inside the foot. Rotate your torso and reach the other arm toward the sky, opening your chest. Hold briefly, then return your hand to the floor. This stretch hits the hips, hamstrings, thoracic spine, and groin all in one movement.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hip flexors, hamstrings, thoracic spine, groin.

levels.name: Add Hamstring Reach
levels.note: Straighten front leg to stretch hamstring
